assumptions.biology: Same-genet contact graft is inspired by controlled Pocillopora damicornis experiments (Collins et al. 2026, doi:10.1126/sciadv.aeh1580). Mechanical contact is verified immediately; tissue fusion, symbiont transfer and recovery over days/weeks remain pending and are not simulated.
assumptions.assistance: Only known same-genet healthy donor fragments may contact bleached but living recipients of the same species proxy. Dead, unknown-genet and mismatched-genet colonies cannot be paired. Red/green fluorescence is a marker for the known simulated lineages, not general genetic identification.
assumptions.substrate: A permanent living recipient branch contacts the donor stem; an abstract pre-existing collar supports the skeleton below the tissue interface. No nearby separate limestone outplant, generated roots or new coral tissue is created at release.
assumptions.scale: The 14 cm visible cutting and robot contact fixture are enlarged engineering proxies for the study's 1–3 cm laboratory fragments. In-situ robotic graft placement and the fixture design are unvalidated extrapolations.
